The square-root size holds only for odd primes p; for p = 2 the sum is 0.
corrected: Sums $\sum e(f(n))$ with $e(x) = e^{2\pi i x}$. Weyl (1916) showed $n^2\alpha$ is equidistributed modulo $1$ for irrational $\alpha$ by squaring the sum (differencing). Complete sums such as $\sum_{n \bmod p} e(n^2/p)$ for an odd prime $p$ have size exactly $\sqrt p$.

corrected: Averages of $|\zeta|^{2k}$ or of $L$-values over families carry information about zeros.
